\[
X=x-4,\qquad Y=y-39 .
\]

The parabola  

\[
2y=x^{2}-8x+12\Longrightarrow y=\frac{(x-4)^{2}-4}{2}
\]

becomes  

\[
y=\frac12X^{2}-2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad Y=\frac12X^{2}-41 .
\tag{1}
\]

The circle of radius \(r\) centred at \((4,39)\) is  

\[
X^{2}+Y^{2}=r^{2}. \tag{2}
\]

---

### Tangency condition  

At a point of tangency the slopes of the two curves are equal.

For the parabola, \(\displaystyle \frac{dy}{dx}=X\).

From (2), implicit differentiation gives  

\[
2X+2Y\,Y'=0\Longrightarrow Y'=-\frac{X}{Y}.
\]

Hence at a common point  

\[
X=-\frac{X}{Y}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad X\bigl(Y+1\bigr)=0 .
\]

Thus either  

* \(X=0\) (the point is on the axis of symmetry), or  
* \(Y=-1\) (i.e. \(y-39=-1\)).

---

### 1.  Case \(X=0\)

From (1) with \(X=0\) we get \(y=-2\).  
The distance from the centre \((4,39)\) to \((4,-2)\) is  

\[
r=|39-(-2)|=41 .
\]

The tangent to the parabola at \((4,-2)\) is horizontal, and a circle with centre \((4,39)\) has a horizontal tangent there as well, so the circle of radius \(41\) is indeed tangent to the parabola at its vertex.

---

### 2.  Case \(Y=-1\)

\(Y=-1\) means \(y=38\).  Substituting this into the parabola equation (1) gives  

\[
38=\frac12X^{2}-2\Longrightarrow X^{2}=80 .
\]

Hence the two symmetric points \(\bigl(\pm\sqrt{80},\,38\bigr)\) lie on the parabola.  
For a point \((X,38)\) the distance to the centre is  

\[
r^{2}=X^{2}+(38-39)^{2}=X^{2}+1=80+1=81,
\]

so \(r=9\).  At those points the slopes of the parabola and the circle are equal (both equal to \(X\)), so the circle of radius \(9\) is tangent to the parabola at the two points \(\bigl(4\pm4\sqrt5,38\bigr)\).

---

No other points can satisfy the slope‑equality condition, so the only possible radii are  

\[
r=9\qquad\text{and}\qquad r=41 .
\]

The sum of all such real numbers \(r\) is  

\[
9+41=50.
\]

\[
\boxed{50}
